import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
import os

# Create output directory if it doesn't exist
os.makedirs('/root/output', exist_ok=True)

# Load all data
water_temp = pd.read_csv('/root/data/water_temperature.csv')
climate = pd.read_csv('/root/data/climate.csv')
land_cover = pd.read_csv('/root/data/land_cover.csv')
hydrology = pd.read_csv('/root/data/hydrology.csv')

# Merge all data by Year
df = water_temp.merge(climate, on='Year') \
    .merge(land_cover, on='Year') \
    .merge(hydrology, on='Year')

print("Data shape:", df.shape)
print("Columns:", df.columns.tolist())
print("\nData preview:")
print(df.head())

# ============================================================================
# PART 1: TREND ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

# Linear regression of WaterTemperature vs Year
years = df['Year'].values
temps = df['WaterTemperature'].values

# Perform linear regression
slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(years, temps)

print(f"\n=== TREND ANALYSIS ===")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f}")
print(f"P-value: {p_value:.6f}")
print(f"R-squared: {r_value**2:.6f}")

# Save trend results
trend_result = pd.DataFrame({
    'slope': [slope],
    'p-value': [p_value]
})
trend_result.to_csv('/root/output/trend_result.csv', index=False)
print("Trend results saved to /root/output/trend_result.csv")

# ============================================================================
# PART 2: DOMINANT FACTOR ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

# Classification of variables into categories
factor_categories = {
    'Heat': ['AirTempLake', 'Shortwave', 'Longwave'],
    'Flow': ['Outflow', 'Inflow'],
    'Wind': ['WindSpeedLake'],
    'Human': ['DevelopedArea', 'AgricultureArea']
}

# For each category, calculate correlation with WaterTemperature
# and assess contribution using relative importance

# First, normalize all predictors for fair comparison
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

# Prepare data for analysis
X = df[['Precip', 'AirTempLake', 'Shortwave', 'Longwave', 'WindSpeedLake',
         'DevelopedArea', 'AgricultureArea', 'Outflow', 'Inflow']].values
y = df['WaterTemperature'].values

scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)

# Fit multiple linear regression
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X_scaled, y)

# Get coefficients
feature_names = ['Precip', 'AirTempLake', 'Shortwave', 'Longwave', 'WindSpeedLake',
                 'DevelopedArea', 'AgricultureArea', 'Outflow', 'Inflow']
coefficients = model.coef_

# Calculate category contributions
category_contributions = {}
category_variables = {}

for category, variables in factor_categories.items():
    indices = [feature_names.index(var) for var in variables if var in feature_names]
    # Sum of absolute coefficient values for this category
    category_coef = np.sum(np.abs(coefficients[indices]))
    category_contributions[category] = category_coef

    # Find which variable in this category has the highest contribution
    if indices:
        max_idx = indices[np.argmax(np.abs(coefficients[indices]))]
        category_variables[category] = feature_names[max_idx]

print(f"\n=== DOMINANT FACTOR ANALYSIS ===")
print("Category contributions (absolute coefficients):")
for category, contrib in sorted(category_contributions.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True):
    print(f"{category}: {contrib:.6f}")

# Find dominant category
dominant_category = max(category_contributions, key=category_contributions.get)
dominant_variable = category_variables[dominant_category]
dominant_coef = category_contributions[dominant_category]

# Calculate percentage contribution
total_contribution = sum(category_contributions.values())
percentage = (dominant_coef / total_contribution) * 100

print(f"\nDominant category: {dominant_category}")
print(f"Most important variable: {dominant_variable}")
print(f"Contribution: {percentage:.2f}%")

# Save dominant factor results
dominant_factor = pd.DataFrame({
    'variable': [dominant_variable],
    'contribution': [percentage]
})
dominant_factor.to_csv('/root/output/dominant_factor.csv', index=False)
print("Dominant factor results saved to /root/output/dominant_factor.csv")

# Also show all category contributions for reference
print("\nAll category percentage contributions:")
for category in sorted(category_contributions.keys(), key=lambda x: category_contributions[x], reverse=True):
    pct = (category_contributions[category] / total_contribution) * 100
    print(f"{category}: {pct:.2f}%")
